Clearly separates the rescuer’s victim from David, the person being rescued.
The unnatural phrase “message that he says will happen” obscures both the speaker and the prophecy.
Tests the command hierarchy rather than confusing the army’s leaders with its muster officials.
Uses an explicit motive and cleanly rejects the incidental size of the king’s offer.
Strongly distinguishes the noise that prompts Athaliah’s movement from what she sees afterward.
Clearly distinguishes Uzziah’s instructor from the father whose conduct he followed.
The explicit first-versus-second covenant contrast makes every participant consequential.
Requires sorting two off-duty companies from the three assigned to other guard posts.
Resolves the outcome to the doubting officer rather than the prophet who warned him.
“What is later reported?” and the answer “the news” are generic and insufficiently informative.
Cleanly distinguishes the weapons’ current giver from their former owner.
Tests the collective defeat of all four rather than Jonathan’s single victory.

The chronology is clear, but the item adds little beyond locating the first of two parallel battle details.

It preserves the plan’s capture-then-entry sequence, though the stem is awkwardly phrased.

Tests the men’s chosen response after explicitly rejecting both remaining and entering the city.

Separates the imagined attackers from the king believed to have hired them.
